<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Intent:** In `@arizeai/phoenix-client`'s `runExperiment`, a task that throws should keep ERROR status on its `Task: ...` span, now with the error message, instead of having it overwritten with OK after the run is logged (#17373).
**Fit:** The `taskFailed` flag stops the late `setStatus(OK)` for failed tasks. The ERROR status now carries the error message, which matches `resumeExperiment`. A patch changeset is included.
**Duplicate:** #17442 (clean99, the reporter of #17373) was opened about 8.5 hours earlier and is still open. It also `resolves #17373`. It changes the same `runTaskWithExamples` status logic by moving `setStatus(OK)` into the try block, and it tests the same success, `"task failed"` and `""` cases in the existing `runExperimentTracing.test.ts`. The only extra thing here is the status `message`, which could be suggested on #17442.
**Verified:** On Node 24.22.2 with pnpm 12, scoped to `phoenix-client`: oxfmt check on changed files passed. `oxlint packages/phoenix-client` failed with 1 error: `typescript(consistent-type-imports)` at `runExperimentTaskSpanStatus.test.ts:17` (`typeof import("@arizeai/phoenix-otel")`). `pnpm run typecheck` passed. `vitest run` passed: 66 files, 642 tests, 1 skipped. With main's `runExperiment.ts` restored, the 2 ERROR cases failed (`expected 1 to be 2`) and the OK case passed.
**Not verified:** Repo-wide `make lint-ts`, `typecheck-ts` and `test-ts`, because only the `phoenix-client` dependency chain was installed. A run against a live Phoenix server.
**Findings without a diff line:** none
**Risk:** side effects low, performance none, backwards compatibility none, from the packages reviewer

Graded against the [review criteria](https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix/blob/main/factory/agents/pr-reviewer.md#verdict).

</details>

review_comments.body:
**Non-blocking.** No test covers the new status message. `runExperiment.ts:611` now sets `span.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.ERROR, message: thisRun.error })`, but the tests only assert `status.code`. If the `message` were dropped, all 3 tests would still pass. That breaks REVIEW.md § Always Check: tests MUST fail when the behavior they cover is removed.

Because of this, the `new Error("")` row only re-checks the `taskFailed` flag.

Fix: also assert `expect(taskSpan().status.message).toBe(error.message)`. That gives `"task failed"` for one row and `""` for the other.
